text.text_excerpt: I had such a great time at this new restaurant in the Saint Hotel that I considered awarding the elusive 5th star. I think before do so, though, I need to go back again which I will shortly do. I was definitely looking forward to trying Sweet Olive since I am a big fan of Coquette. Suite Olive did not disappoint. The food, the wine, the service were all fantastic. It does have a little bit of a sterile look about it and it is right at the front door of the hotel which is one of the reasons I deducted a star. I just don't like hotel restaurants plopped in the middle of lobby. Ultimately the ambience became an nonfactor once the food and wine came out. I dined with 3 other companions and we...

I came here with a group of friends for a birthday dinner. I must say the whole atmosphere and decor of the place is amazing. Very classy and and modern. The restaurant is part of a hotel which is seprated by these bueitiful white curtains. I also liked how the area included a bar, pool table, and a section for a live band. As a group we all ordered the mussels, ravioli, pork belly, and boudin balls for appetizers. All of them tasted great, but my favorite would have to be the pork belly. For my entree I ordered the pork chop. The size was fairly decent and the sauce for it was good too. For dessert we all got the mud pie, lemon berry tart, and strawberry cake. Sweet Olive (actually their name recently changed to Tempt) offered my group and I a wonderful experience, though the wait for the food were at times excruciating. Let's start with the ambiance and decor: I loved it! Ultra chic and modern with white and clear furniture and decor. The restaurant is rather small and is separated from the rest of a hotel by long white curtains hanging from the ceiling. The chandeliers and candelabras above and on the tables were also a good touch. Tempt offers a small menu, with only four appetizers, four entrees, and I believe four or five salads to choose from.
